resolution: Fixed the mirrored-quad shape mismatch the user reported (left face convex, right face concave, mismatched white/gray shading despite identical mirrored vertices). Root cause: editMeshToGeometry fan-triangulated every face from loop[0], which for a quad always cuts the loop[0]->loop[2] diagonal. A mirror twin's loop is reflected AND reversed, so the same rule cut the OTHER diagonal — a non-planar quad buckled one way on the left and the opposite way on the right. Added quadTriPositions(), which chooses a quad's diagonal purely from geometry and the outward face normal (prefer the diagonal whose two tris both stay convex — the same rule Split Quads uses; tiebreak on the shorter diagonal), both reflection-invariant so a face and its twin pick corresponding diagonals. Wired it into editMeshToGeometry (fixes both the live Studio viewport and the cooked/baked asset, which share that lowering) and refactored splitQuad to reuse the same helper so the split matches what is rendered. Added a regression test proving a quad and its reflected+reversed twin fold along corresponding diagonals; editMesh 102/102, cookedAsset 26/26, meshPaint 15/15 green.
